methodological_rigor.justification: AXINET is an international randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, double-dummy phase II-III trial in 256 patients with advanced grade 1-2 extrapancreatic NETs, with stratified central randomization by primary site, Ki-67 (5% cutoff), and time from diagnosis. BICR was performed retrospectively in 94.9% of patients with characteristics similar to the overall population (Table S2). The authors transparently report that the primary endpoint (investigator-assessed PFS) was not met, acknowledge baseline imbalances (more ECOG PS ≥1, grade 2, lung/colorectal tumors in the axitinib arm) and provide a multivariable adjusted analysis. Main methodological concern is the mid-study redesign from phase II to phase II-III and that PFS in the control arm (13.1 months) substantially exceeded the 2-year 28% assumption used for sample-size planning, reducing power.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase III trial (Oxford 1b) in an orphan indication (epNETs) where treatment options remain limited. Although the primary endpoint was missed, the BICR-assessed PFS (16.6 v 9.9 months; HR 0.71; P=.017) and substantial ORR advantage (17.5% v 4.6% investigator; 12.8% v 3.2% BICR) provide clinically meaningful activity data. Relevance is tempered by the subsequent approval of cabozantinib (CABINET) as the first TKI for epNETs, which limits the potential for axitinib to change practice.

reporting_quality.justification: Figure 1 is a CONSORT diagram; the manuscript registers the trial (EudraCT 2011-001550-29; NCT01744249), reports eligibility, randomization, blinding, endpoints, and statistical assumptions including O'Brien-Fleming boundaries with Lan-DeMets spending. AEs are tabulated by grade and serious/fatal events are itemized. Reporting of the phase II to III redesign and acknowledgment of primary endpoint failure are commendable. No explicit data-sharing statement is visible in the provided text, and several subgroup and BICR details are deferred to the Data Supplement.

novelty_literature.justification: Axitinib had prior phase II signal in NETs (Strosberg 2016) and multiple antiangiogenic TKIs (sunitinib, lenvatinib, pazopanib, surufatinib, cabozantinib) have been studied in NETs. The authors appropriately frame AXINET as the first European randomized trial of an angiogenesis inhibitor in epNETs and the first worldwide TKI-SSA combination trial. The incremental contribution is meaningful for an orphan disease but is a class-consistent confirmation rather than a novel mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with detailed methods, transparent reporting of a negative primary endpoint alongside positive secondary/BICR endpoints, and a discussion that honestly addresses investigator-BICR discrepancy (RECIST limitations for hypervascular liver metastases, Choi criteria) and the evolving landscape (cabozantinib CABINET, surufatinib SANET-ep). Tables 1-2, Figures 1-4, and the limitations section are thorough. Text is dense but readable.

key_strengths: Double-blind, double-dummy placebo-controlled randomized design in an orphan indication with stratified central randomization
Retrospective BICR in 94.9% of patients showing PFS benefit (HR 0.71; P=.017) and significant ORR advantage on both investigator and central assessment
Transparent reporting of negative primary endpoint with honest discussion of control-arm PFS exceeding planning assumptions and investigator-BICR discrepancy
Appropriate multivariable adjustment for baseline imbalances and prespecified subgroup analyses
key_concerns: Primary endpoint (investigator-assessed PFS) was not met; positive conclusions rest on secondary and post hoc BICR analyses
Mid-study phase II to III redesign and long accrual window (2011-2019) with evolving NET standard of care during enrollment
Baseline imbalances in ECOG PS, grade distribution, and primary site potentially biasing results against the axitinib arm
No explicit data/code availability statement in the main text
Subsequent approval of cabozantinib for epNETs limits practice-changing impact
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-conducted randomized placebo-controlled trial in an orphan disease with transparent reporting and meaningful secondary signals despite missing the primary endpoint; tier 1 oncology journal acceptance is plausible with minor revisions given the rarity of randomized data in epNETs.
